terms.scope_claimed: the name 'CIRISHolon' / 'holon' for this object, and the specific combination: the closed view with a certified witness-pair failure, admission of a tier by carriage with a stated price, and the engine built on it with preregistered kills
terms.scope_note: The commuting square and closure are standard (Simon 1962; Simon and Ando 1961; Kemeny and Snell 1960; Park 1981; Milner; Cousot and Cousot 1977; Mori–Zwanzig; Wilson and Kadanoff; TICA/VAMP; Barnett and Seth; Rosas et al.; Shalizi and Crutchfield; Tishby et al. 1999). 'Holon' was coined by Koestler (1967), drawing on Simon. Six Birds (Tsiokos, 2026) is convergent independent work. CIRIS claims only the name and the specific combination.

terms.scope_claimed: the application of the CIRIS holon as a reality compiler: a physical model carried tier by tier, each tier certified against the tier below for what the level above reads, within a stated budget, with refusal by name where no certificate exists
terms.scope_note: Certification is relative to a derived model, not to nature. Compiler correctness as a commuting diagram is classical (McCarthy and Painter 1967; Morris 1973), as are bisimulation, abstract interpretation and lumpability. CIRIS claims nothing on the bare phrase or the square; it claims the application from 2026-08-26 and the compound 'CIRIS reality compiler' from this record.
